# Ember Rail, round 2: harsh critique and build list

Worktree `/Users/moshe/Developer/RbxAI-design2`, branch `design/round-2`. No source files edited and nothing committed. Evidence is untracked at `docs/evidence/ember-rail-round2/` (272 JPEGs, 48 MB, plus metrics JSON and the capture scripts in `metrics/`). I left it uncommitted because of the size, so tell me if you want it committed.

**Setup and method.** Capture and probe scripts are `shoot-site.mjs`, `shoot-app.mjs` and `perf.mjs` in `metrics/`. The rest were one-off probes and are not saved.
- I symlinked `node_modules` into the worktree for `.`, `apps/site`, `apps/web`, `apps/worker`, `packages/corpus` and `packages/evals`. `packages/design` has none in the main checkout, so I removed that dangling link. These links are untracked.
- I built the site with astro (21 pages) and ran the app under vite dev with `?mock=1`.
- Login, signup and forgot only render without mock mode, because mock mode always has a session. I captured those three without it.
- I did not run the test suite.

**Spec gap.** `D-EMBER-1` is not in `docs/DECISIONS.md` in this worktree. I used the Ember spec in commit messages `3d700c14`, `7846a971` and `9054403a`, and the token sheets.

**Defects I could not fully confirm.**
- Loading states: I read them in code, but mock data resolves instantly, so I did not capture a skeleton.
- Hover and active states, RTL, and `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour: not captured or tested.
- Light mode: I eyeballed the app dashboard, workspace, usage and settings in light, and the site programmatically. I did not review the other light captures page by page.
- Perf numbers are a Playwright proxy, not Lighthouse. It is not installed, and I did not try `npx --no-install lighthouse`.

## Screenshot index

Base: `docs/evidence/ember-rail-round2/`

- **Site:** `site/<page>-<1440|768|390>-<dark|light>.jpg`, full page after scrolling through, 126 files. The page key is `landing`, `pricing`, `docs`, `docs_<name>`, `models`, `proof`, `status`, `changelog`, `discord`, `privacy`, `terms`, `404`.
- **No-scroll captures:** `landing-*-asis.jpg` and `pricing-*-asis.jpg` are taken at 0.5 s with no scrolling.
- **Reproductions:**
  - `site/pricing-1440-dark-fullpage-after-scroll-2300.jpg` (the header-in-the-middle bug)
  - `site/landing-1440-dark-fullpage-3.5s.jpg`
  - `site/landing-1440-dark-fullpage-cv-visible.jpg`
- **App:** `app/<route>-<width>-<theme>.jpg` is the viewport. `-full` is a full-page capture, taken only when the page scrolls past 1000 px (not for the workspace). `workspace-*-t8s.jpg` is 8 s in.
- **App routes:** `dashboard`, `workspace`, `roadmap`, `branding`, `usage`, `settings`, `admin`, `ui-lab` (dev only), `join`, `notfound`, `recovery`, `reset`, `confirm`, `login`, `signup`, `forgot`.
- **690 px repro:** `app/dashboard-690-dark.jpg`.
- **Raw numbers:** `metrics/site-dom.json`, `metrics/app-dom-all.json`, `metrics/perf-proxy.json`.

## Today's reported defects, resolved

1. **Pricing "header in the middle" and visible "Skip to content" is a capture artifact, with a real cause underneath.**
   - The header is `position: sticky` and is at y=0 in every capture taken at scrollY=0.
   - I reproduced the bug by scrolling to y=2300 and then taking a full-page capture. The header and the skip link both draw at that scroll offset (`pricing-1440-dark-fullpage-after-scroll-2300.jpg`).
   - The skip link is `position: fixed; top: 12px` hidden only by `translateY(-67.8px)`, so it sits just above the viewport. It shows in any full-page capture taken while scrolled.
   - Fix the cause: hide it with `clip-path` or `visibility` until `:focus`, not by being off-screen.
   - A full-page capture should also scroll to the top first.

2. **The long empty bands are two separate things.**
   - **Blank until the reveal fires.** Everything marked `[data-reveal]` starts at `opacity: 0` and waits for an IntersectionObserver, with a 2.6 s failsafe (`Landing.astro`, `Base.astro`).
     - A capture at 0.5 s shows the whole page empty below the hero: `landing-1440-dark-asis.jpg`, `pricing-1440-dark-asis.jpg`.
     - Pricing's 1,259 px "compare" section is blank in `pricing-1440-dark.jpg`.
   - **Still blank after the failsafe.** `#models` and `.closing` have `content-visibility: auto` (`landing.css:453`). They stay blank in full-page captures even at 3.5 s. Overriding that one rule makes both bands render (`landing-1440-dark-fullpage-cv-visible.jpg`).
   - Even rendered, `#models` is one card, and `/models` is one card in a 493 px section.
   - **Fix:** content must be visible by default. Animate only with CSS scroll-driven animation behind `@supports`, with no JS gating. Remove `content-visibility: auto` or give it a true intrinsic size.

3. **The 690 px menu overlap is real, and the "invisible card" is not stuck.**
   - The fixed "Open navigation" button sits at (9,9)–(55,55) and overlaps the `h1` (top at y=44).
   - I measured it at 690, 768, 820 and 900 on `/` and `/usage`. It was not present at 600 or 1000. On `/settings` it overlaps at 768, 820 and 900 but not at 690.
   - 768 px is iPad portrait.
   - Project-card opacity during the entrance stagger was 0.87, 0.60 and 0.12 at 150 ms. All three reached 1.00 by 600 ms at 600, 690 and 820 px. A capture at about 150 ms looks broken, so cap the stagger and never hide a card for more than about 100 ms.

4. **Workspace tour card.**
   - It sits over the last message at 1440 and 390 px (`workspace-1440-dark.jpg`, `workspace-390-dark.jpg`).
   - At 390 a third layer, the "Studio connected" toast, overlaps both the tour card and the composer.

5. **Syntax highlighting contrast.** Measured against the code background in the workspace:

   | Theme | Token | Ratio |
   |---|---|---|
   | Dark | comment `#6a737d` | 3.54 |
   | Light | keyword `#d73a49` | 4.01 |
   | Light | comment | 4.22 |

   Code font size is 11.31 px.

## Performance (Playwright proxy, localhost, gzip, cold)

The mobile profile throttles to 1.6 Mbps down, 150 ms RTT and 4x CPU. Each figure is the median of 3 runs.

| Page | Desktop FCP/LCP | Throttled mobile FCP/LCP | Transfer | CLS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 56 ms | 560 ms | 36.7 KB | 0 |
| `/pricing` | 40 ms | 500 ms | 21.2 KB | 0.0187 desktop |
| `/docs/getting-started` | 44 ms | 460 ms | 16.2 KB | 0 |
| `/proof` | 44 ms | 452 ms | 12.8 KB | 0 |
| **`/app/login`** | 56 / 68 ms | **2,052 / 2,084 ms** | **326.9 KB** (264.7 JS + 61.1 CSS) | 0 |

- The public site is already light. `check-landing-budget` passes at 16,593 of 20,000 B gzip, 17,398 B of inline JS, and 27,016 B of images.
- **The pricing layout shift is real.** `.plan-rail` moves 62 px at about 50 ms, CLS 0.0187. It showed in about 11 of 14 desktop runs and was 0 in a few.
- **Workspace chunk: the biggest finding.**
  - The workspace is already `lazy()`, but Rollup named its chunk `mermaid-HWGCJPDP-*.js`. It is 2,390,857 B raw and 690,100 B gzip.
  - By sourcemap it contains mermaid (480 KB raw), katex (260 KB), react-jsx-parser (242 KB), parse5, marked, streamdown and shiki.
  - Fetching it on the throttled profile took 3,477 ms. The Suspense fallback during that wait is an empty `<div class="page" aria-busy>`, one of 8 such fallbacks in `app.tsx`.
  - So `check-app-bundle`'s "/workspace has no chunk of its own" is a naming false positive. The real problem is that the chunk is a monolith.
- **Entry chunk:** 182,795 B gzip against the 150,000 B budget. Sourcemap attribution:

  | Source | Raw size |
  |---|---|
  | react-dom | 177 KB |
  | app source | 240 KB |
  | motion-dom + framer-motion + motion-utils | 124.5 KB |
  | tailwind-merge | 27.6 KB |

  - The `motion` library is imported only by `components/ai-elements/shimmer.tsx`. Replacing that with a CSS shimmer should remove roughly 40 to 45 KB gzip. That is my estimate from compressing the sliced code, not a measured result. It would bring the entry to about 140 KB, which should pass the budget. Measure it after the change.
- **Other chunks fetched on the throttled profile:** `settings` took 297 ms (29,724 B gzip). `usage` took 212 ms (10,996 B).
- **Eager CSS:** 503,425 B total across files, about 89.8 KB gzip, including 334 KB raw in the main stylesheet.

## Critique: public site

The ratings are against the owner's brief ("landing-page quality") and the Ember spec. Hairlines, tokens and the type stack are correct everywhere, and no page overflows horizontally at any width. That is where the praise ends.

**Landing `/`** (`landing-*`) is C+. It is the only page designed rather than re-tokened.
- **The Baseplate toy.** It is a 9×5 grid of hollow rings at 1440 (6×4 at 390), which reads as a form, not a toy.
  - At 390 each cell is 48×58, so the studs stretch into tall ellipses.
  - No brick, no depth, no motion at rest, no hint of the first action.
- **Rhythm.** About 800 px between bands holding 3 to 5 lines each. 6,056 px tall at 1440 and 9,193 px at 390.
- **Content.**
  - "Sent, both times" is a monospace log in a bare column.
  - The cycle diagram is four squares and a rule.
  - "What it is good at" is four identical cards with an icon square.
  - The `#built` figure is a tiny thumbnail of an inventory screen.
  - There is no hero visual beyond the toy, so the first screen is a headline, a composer and rings.
- **Motion.** Only the 8 px `rise` entrance and the loop that lights once. No scroll-linked life and no hover-state evidence captured.
- **Rail.** The Rail's five nodes are good, and on mobile it folds to a 2 px bar.
- **Dead space.** The empty bands from the section above.

**Pricing** is C+. Good content, document layout.
- 33 to 37 fully round elements, and 12 text nodes under 12 px.
- Plan cards are the same card three times, with a dashed "Checkout not open" button as the only differentiator.
- The comparison table is a plain `<table>` with no sticky first column.
- The layout shift above.
- Static "Skip to content" artifact.

**Docs index and 10 `/docs/*` pages** are D+ on design, B on legibility. They are the DocsLayout chassis, re-tokened.
- Left nav with a search field, a prose column, 13 to 21 fully round elements per page, 5 text nodes under 12 px.
- `getting-started` has 12 text nodes under 12 px.
- The Folder pick is a large flat orange folder with "Open the folder to see what is inside", which is off-language.
- At 390 the nav is a `<details>` "Docs navigation" selector.
- No code-block design, no callout system, no per-page progress, and no motion. The footer repeats the whole docs link set.

**Models `/models`** is D. A single card in a 493 px section, "Apple / Builds complete Roblox games from a short prompt", then the footer.

**Proof** is C. Content-rich, but the "Reads first / Undo point / …" chips are pill chips, and the run log is monospace walls. It needs the Ember log or terminal component.

**Status** is C. One card and a list of known issues. It has 1 console error because the health endpoint 404s on the static server, so I'm not counting it as a defect.

**Changelog** is C. The "Update" and "v0.2" version chips are pills. The long dated list is good content with no timeline structure.

**Privacy and Terms** are D+ legal prose in the LegalLayout chassis. They are long and flat, with no table of contents on mobile.

**404** is D. A centred headline and two buttons in a 612 px band, a bare error state. This is the cheapest place for the brick, and it shows nothing.

**Discord** is a redirect page. The capture shows an external page, with 9 to 10 console errors from discord.com that are not ours. Nothing to design except the "Join the server" fallback.

**Site-wide**
- Source has 46 `backdrop-filter` declarations across 14 files. Live blur is only 1 to 2 elements per page, which meets the spec.
- No cross-document view transitions. No link prefetch. Reveal and failsafe are duplicated in two layouts.

## Critique: app

The app is the weakest area. It is re-tokened, not redesigned.

| Route | Rating | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard `/` | C | Three bordered cards (name, two-line description, place, "updated 2h ago") in a two-column grid. No thumbnail, status, last-run or usage glance. The composer, the best idea on the landing page, is absent. The page is half empty below the cards. `ProjectSignature` still carries the retired flow-field "contour lines" language (`dashboard.tsx:1144`). |
| Workspace | C- | The densest page. The topbar repeats "Ember Halls" twice at every width. It has no `<h1>`. An unstyled error line, "We could not check your access — reload to try again", renders in the thread. This line appears in mock mode and may be a mock artifact; I did not isolate it, but it shows the error state has no design. |
| Usage | C | Good bones: a ring, a sparkline and an activity calendar. Uses 3 px radii (40 elements) and 2 px radii, off the 4/6/10/14/20 ladder. |
| Settings | C- | A nested tab-pill nav (`st-nav__link`). At 390 the heading is indented relative to the search box and the tab row clips at "Notifications". The settings page logs 401 and 404 responses in mock mode. |
| Login, signup, forgot | D+ | Not designed. The email field is autofocused, so the Ember ring shows on load. The primary button reads as muddy brown, because it is disabled at 100% (the disabled colour is the 50% Ember). A decorative dot sits above the logo. Nothing is shown beside the card. |
| Recovery, reset, confirm, join | D+ | Centred cards in a void. |
| 404 (app) | D | "This apple is lost" with the outline-cube glyph is fine, but it is a bare centred state. |
| Roadmap | C | Rich content (breadcrumb, progress strip, "What is in this place" panel with stats, scan notices) in small type. The List/Map toggle is a tiny pill. Has 41 text nodes under 12 px. |
| Branding | D | Showed only "This project was not found" in mock mode. It logs a 404. |
| Admin | C- | Operator tool. It uses weight 700 (13 text nodes ≥ 650). |

**Spec violations measured on rendered pages**
- **Weights.** Computed weights on the dashboard are 400, 450, 480, 500, 520 and 600 (six values). Admin and roadmap use 700.
- **Type size.** Elements under 12 px, and total sizes in use:

  | Page | Elements under 12 px |
  |---|---|
  | Dashboard | 10 |
  | Workspace | 53 (38 are code tokens at 11.31 px) |
  | Roadmap | 41 |
  | Settings | 9 |
  | `ui-lab` (dev only) | 176 |

  In source, 122 CSS `font-size` declarations are under 12 px, with 10 px on `.gx-composer__note` and `.gx-usage__plan`.
- **Gradients and blur.** Gradients live at rest only on the workspace: `.gx-compose-region`, `.pk-glow` and one toolbar div. Live blur is 3 elements on the workspace (topbar, composer, and a floating toolbar) and 1 to 2 on settings.
- **Pointer-following effects.** `press-fx.css` carries the spotlight and `dashboard.css:499` writes `--card-x/--card-y` on pointermove. `orb.tsx`, `border-glow.tsx` and `magnetic-dock.ts` also listen to pointermove. Those effects only appear on hover or focus.
- **Source gradients.** 36 `gradient(` uses across 12 CSS files in `apps/web`, 9 of them in `design/system.css`.
- **Radii.** The workspace uses 8 px (8 elements), `999px` and `33554400px` pills (16 elements); settings uses 9 px (8 elements). All are off the ladder.
- **Per-route titles.** `document.title` is identical on every route ("Apple — build Roblox games inside Studio") and no source sets it. The route is invisible to browser history, tab switchers and assistive tech.
- **Targets.** 24 controls under 44 px in the workspace at 390, 7 in the dashboard at 390.

**Missing motion and states**
- No route transition, in the app or between site pages.
- Lazy routes show an empty busy `<div>` (8 fallbacks in `app.tsx`).
- The dashboard has a skeleton `card-grid` with `aria-busy`. The workspace chunk wait has nothing.
- Empty states exist (`empty-state.tsx`), but I did not capture any beyond join and 404.
- Error states are minimal: `failure.tsx` exists, but the access-check error renders as plain text.
- Loading components (`Forge`, `Spinner`) carry the owner's "picks": warp field, code rain, ripple, infinity path. Those pick styles are gradient-heavy and not in Ember language.

## THE gimmick: "The Plate"

**Name and idea.** The Plate is one object that appears in three places and always means the same thing: the bricks on it are real. It grows from the existing Baseplate, the Snap logo stud and the Rail, so the Baseplate toy evolves into it.

**1. Landing.** Replace the hollow rings with a studded plate that has depth.
- **Depth without gradients.** A stud is a filled circle with a 2 px darker plate edge below it (`--plate`). A brick is its hue with a 2 px edge and a hard 0-blur side face, stacked at 4 px per level, up to the existing 3-high cap.
- **Cue.** One Ember target ring on the first stud, pulsing twice, to say where to start.
- **Stamps.** Three buttons (Row, Square, Stairs) that place bricks when clicked.
  - They are the visitor's own action. The existing honesty rule holds: no pre-built layout, no replay.
  - The existing "Describe this to Apple" bridge writes the sentence into the composer and never submits.
- **Snap feel.** Drop 6 px and settle in 90 ms with `--ease-snap`. The logo stud clicks on the same beat. Sound is opt-in only (the existing `interface-sound.ts` pattern, off by default). `navigator.vibrate(8)` on touch.
- **Size.** Cells stay square at every width. The 390 fix is `aspect-ratio: 1` with the grid set by columns.

**2. Carry-over.** The plate persists in `sessionStorage` (the site's plate does already).
- Render a small read-only copy in the site footer, and on signup offer "Start your first project from this plate". That pre-fills the new-project sentence for the user to edit. Nothing is sent without their action.
- The app is served under `/app/` on the same host. I read that from `base: '/app/'` and did not test cross-page sessionStorage in production, so confirm it.

**3. In the app.** Every project owns a Plate that replaces the `ProjectSignature` contour lines.
- One brick per real checkpoint, from the checkpoint list the workspace already provides through `useProvideCheckpoints`.
- Hue by run kind, four hues, positions from a hash of the checkpoint id. Same id, same brick, forever.
- Capped at 24 bricks, with "+N" beyond that.
- An empty project shows an empty plate of studs, an honest zero.
- When a new checkpoint arrives while you watch, the brick drops with the Snap click.
- Every plate has an accessible name like "12 checkpoints" and a tooltip: "One brick per checkpoint Apple took in this project."

**Share.** "Save plate as image" does an SVG-to-canvas PNG export on click only, lazy-loaded. It has bricks and a "Made with Apple" line, and sends no data.

**Fast and accessible**
- DOM and SVG only, no canvas or WebGL on the page.
- Landing script budget 6 KB gzip, up from 3.0 KB. The app part is at most 1.5 KB gzip in the entry.
- A placement is one DOM write.
- Animation uses only `transform` and `opacity`.
- Reduced motion: bricks appear instantly and nothing pulses.
- Keyboard and screen reader: keep the roving-tabindex grid, the live region, and the 44 px studs.
- The toy hides entirely without scripting.
- Labelled as a toy, always. It never claims Apple built anything.

## Prioritised build list

**Track A: site pages**
1. Reveal and visibility: content visible by default; CSS scroll-driven reveal behind `@supports`; delete `content-visibility: auto` on `#models` and `.closing`; make the skip link hidden by `clip-path` or `visibility`.
2. Pricing `.plan-rail` shift (CLS 0.0187 to 0). Differentiate the plan cards. Give the comparison table a sticky first column.
3. Landing: compress the band rhythm. Replace the "same request" log, the cycle diagram and the four-card grid with Ember components. Give the hero a real visual (the Plate).
4. A shared Ember docs shell replacing DocsLayout and LegalLayout. It needs a code block, callouts, a table of contents, prev/next, an in-page search result style, and no pill chips or off-language folder illustration. Roll it through the 11 docs pages, privacy and terms.
5. Models, proof, changelog and status: a real model/engine page and a structured timeline for the changelog and the proof log.
6. 404 and the discord fallback: designed pages with the Plate and a brick.
7. Remove pill and round chips in favour of the 4/6/10/14/20 ladder. Raise the 12 px text nodes to 12 px or more.

**Track B: app pages and components**
1. **Fix the 640–999 px overlap.** Give the nav button its own top bar or reserved padding, so it never overlaps a heading (measured 690–900).
2. Dashboard: a composer-first "what do you want to build" entry, cards with a Plate and a status line, and recent activity and a usage glance.
3. Workspace: dock the tour so it never covers messages or the composer. Resolve the 3-layer overlap at 390. Add a real `<h1>`. Remove the duplicate "Ember Halls". Style the access-error line. Fix code colours to AA in both themes: dark comments to 4.5:1 and light `local` and comments to 4.5:1.
4. Settings, usage, login, signup, forgot, recovery, reset, confirm and join: redesign against the Ember spec. A real auth layout (brand panel and the Plate), no autofocus ring on load, and the primary button's disabled state not drawn as a dim fill.
5. Remove pointer-following spotlights, gradients and `backdrop-filter` beyond the topbar and the composer. Remove sub-12 px text and weights above 600. Collapse the weights to 400, 500 and 600, and the radii onto the ladder.
6. Per-route `document.title`. 44 px targets on mobile controls.
7. Skeletons for lazy routes in place of the empty fallback.

**Track C: motion system, gimmick, performance budget**
1. **Bundle.**
   - Replace the Shimmer `motion` import with a CSS shimmer. Re-measure the entry. My estimate is about 140 KB against the 150 KB budget; it is not measured.
   - Lazy-load mermaid, katex, react-jsx-parser and shiki languages on first use. Target the workspace chunk at 250 KB gzip or less, from 690 KB.
   - Name the workspace chunk (`manualChunks` or `chunkFileNames`) so `check-app-bundle`'s workspace check stops giving a false failure.
2. **Motion tokens and primitives:**
   - Enter (rise 8 px and fade, 160 ms).
   - Press feedback on every button with the 2 px plate edge.
   - List stagger capped at 240 ms.
   - A shared skeleton primitive sized to the final layout, so there are no layout jumps.
   - Cross-document view transitions on the site and same-document view transitions on app routes.
   - Prefetch on hover, focus and touch in the site, and idle-preload the workspace chunk after the dashboard.
3. Build the Plate: landing, carry-over, then the app project plate.
4. **Budgets:** landing at most 45 KB total (36.7 KB today). Other site pages at most 25 KB. LCP at most 1.0 s on the throttled proxy (landing 0.56 s today). CLS 0. `/app/login` first load at most 200 KB gzip (327 KB today). Entry at most 150,000 B gzip. Eager CSS at most 40 KB gzip (about 90 KB today). Add the throttled-proxy perf script as a check.

## Recap
- **Milestone:** none, ad-hoc work (round-2 design review).
- **Phase:** n/a
- **Stage:** discussed
- **Why:** the owner wants to see the whole website redesigned at landing-page quality, so this review sets the build list.
- **Building:** a measured critique and a three-track build list, with no source changes.
- **Next:** orchestrator picks the starting track. Suggested start is Track C's bundle fixes plus Track A item 1, which are measurable and unblock the rest.
